title: AI music has surpassed 50% of new music uploads
measure: Fully AI-generated tracks as % of daily uploads to Deezer (own detector)
latest_value: >50% of uploads, ~90,000 tracks/day (Jun 2026); 13.4m AI tracks tagged in 2025
finding: AI share of daily uploads rose from about 10% (Jan 2025) to over 50% (Jun 2026).
limits: one platform's own detector; Deezer markets itself against AI music; release gives 90,000 as both daily and monthly figure

title: AI music share of streams and fraud share
measure: % of Deezer streams going to fully AI-generated tracks; % of those streams flagged fraudulent
latest_value: 1–3% of streams (Jul 2026); up to 85% of AI-track streams fraudulent (2025)
finding: AI tracks get 1–3% of streams, up from about 0.5% in Nov 2025, and up to 85% of those streams were fraudulent in 2025.
limits: reported as a range, not a point; fraud classification is Deezer's own

title: Deezer/Ipsos survey on AI music
measure: % of adults who could not tell fully AI music from human-made in a blind test (9,000 adults, 8 countries)
finding: 97% of listeners could not tell fully AI-generated tracks from human-made ones in a blind test.
limits: commissioned by an interested platform; short clips

title: AI now writes as many online articles as humans
measure: % of new English web articles (Common Crawl, article schema, 100+ words) classed primarily AI by 3 detectors averaged
finding: Primarily-AI articles rose from a 1.4–1.8% false-positive floor to about 50% by late 2024 and have stayed near 50% for five quarters.
limits: SEO vendor; detector-dependent (method change moved level 3.3 points); no Q2 2026 point published

title: AI content in Google search results
measure: % of Google top-20 results for 500 informational keywords classed AI
finding: AI share of top Google results rose from about 7% (Mar 2024) to 17–20% in 2025, then stopped being updated after Sep 2025.
limits: detector vendor; small keyword set; tracker appears discontinued (no point after Sep 2025 as of Oct 2026)

title: What percentage of new content is AI-generated?
measure: % of 900,000 newly detected English pages with any / pure AI text
finding: 74% of new pages contained some AI text but only 2.5% were purely AI, showing how much the headline depends on threshold.
limits: vendor detector; one page per domain

title: AI slop writing has taken over the internet, particularly LinkedIn and X
measure: % of long posts (250+ words) classed fully AI, by platform, from users of Pangram's browser extension
latest_value: LinkedIn 41%, X 25%, Substack 21.9%, Reddit posts 11.6%, Reddit comments 1.9% (Apr–Jul 2026)
finding: Fully AI text was 41% of long LinkedIn posts but under 2% of Reddit comments.
limits: detector vendor; self-selected extension users; long posts only

title: AI Slop Report: The Global Rise of Low-Quality AI Videos
measure: Share of first 500 Shorts served to a new YouTube account that were AI slop; AI slop channels among top 100 trending channels per country
latest_value: 104 of 500 Shorts (21%) AI slop; 165 (33%) brainrot (Oct 2025 data)
finding: 21% of the first 500 Shorts shown to a new account were AI slop, and AI slop channels were among the top 100 trending channels in many countries (e.g. 9 in the US).
limits: one fresh account; manual coding; video-editing vendor; cannot separate algorithm from upload volume

title: AI artists on Billboard charts
measure: Count of AI or AI-assisted acts that have appeared on any Billboard chart
finding: AI acts on Billboard charts went from 2 in 2023 to 12 by mid-Nov 2025, mostly on niche sales and emerging-artist charts.
limits: count of acts, not share of listening; niche charts; list not updated after Nov 2025

title: Spotify strengthens AI protections for artists, songwriters and producers
measure: Spammy tracks removed in 12 months; AI policies (impersonation, spam filter, DDEX AI credits)
latest_value: >75 million spammy tracks removed (12 months to Sep 2025)
finding: Spotify removed over 75 million spammy tracks in a year and introduced AI disclosures that it says will not lead to down-ranking; it published no AI share of uploads or listening.
limits: spam is not all AI; no AI share reported

title: TikTok lets users choose how much AI content they see
measure: Platform policy: user control over AI-generated content in For You feed; invisible watermarking
finding: TikTok began testing a control to reduce AI-generated content in feeds but published no count or share of AI content.
limits: paperwork only; no numbers

title: Almost half of the images on Adobe Stock are AI-generated
measure: AI-generated images as share of Adobe Stock collection
finding: AI images made up almost half of the Adobe Stock collection by April 2025, by a contributor's count that Adobe disputes.
limits: one blogger's count; method not described; Adobe disputes

title: AI and the Quantity and Quality of Creative Products: Have LLMs Boosted Creation of Valuable Books? (NBER WP 34777)
measure: AI share of new English ebook releases on Amazon (Pangram on 1,000-word previews, 48,193 titles); usage via ratings and sales rank
latest_value: AI ('not fully human') share 23.1% (2023), 33.6% (2024), 52.7% (2025); monthly releases ~3x 2022
finding: Monthly ebook releases nearly tripled and over half of 2025 releases contained AI text, but AI books get far less use (raw average ratings 6.0 vs 82.5) and human-authored output held steady.
limits: vendor detector; 'not fully human' includes light AI help; ebooks only; usage gap narrowing

title: Generative AI floods and dilutes the market for books
measure: Sales share of self-published genre-fiction books with >25% detected AI text (14,419 books, daily sales to Jun 2026)
latest_value: ~20% of sales by 2026 Q2 (press report; abstract gives no figure); titles selling per quarter up 19.2x vs revenue 8.9x
finding: AI-heavy books' share of sales grows over time and books with no AI text lose most ground in high-AI genres; revenue per selling book fell in most genres.
limits: preprint; observational; self-published genre fiction only; 20% figure via Let's Data Science, not read in paper

title: Pangram predicts 21% of ICLR reviews are AI-generated
measure: % of ICLR 2026 peer reviews (≈70,000) classed fully AI-generated
latest_value: 21% fully AI (15,899 reviews); over half some AI involvement (Nov 2025)
finding: 21% of ICLR 2026 reviews were classed fully AI-generated, against 6.5–16.9% AI-modified review text estimated for 2023–24 venues by Liang et al.
limits: detector vendor's own analysis; one venue; different method from Liang et al.

title: Delving into LLM-assisted writing in biomedical publications through excess vocabulary
measure: Lower-bound % of PubMed abstracts processed with LLMs (excess-vocabulary method, 15m abstracts 2010–2024)
finding: At least 13.5% of 2024 biomedical abstracts were LLM-processed, up to 40% in some subgroups.
limits: ends 2024; style-word method may miss newer models; also in group.jsonl

title: The widespread adoption of large language model-assisted writing across society
measure: Estimated % of documents LLM-assisted: consumer complaints, corporate and UN press releases, job postings
latest_value: complaints ~18%, corporate press releases ~24%, UN press releases ~14%, small-firm job posts ~10% (to 2024)
finding: LLM-assisted writing rose fast after ChatGPT to 10–24% across genres and stabilised by 2024.
limits: series end 2023–24; lower bounds; includes polishing and translation

title: Quantifying large language model usage in scientific papers
measure: Estimated LLM-modified share of paper abstracts/introductions by field (1.12m papers, 2020–Sep 2024)
latest_value: up to 22% computer science; up to 9% mathematics (Sep 2024)
finding: LLM-modified text reached up to 22% in computer-science papers by Sep 2024, lowest in mathematics.
limits: ends 2024; distributional estimate

title: Human-LLM Coevolution: Evidence from Academic Writing
measure: Frequency of ChatGPT-favoured words in arXiv abstracts over time
latest_value: 'delve' and other flagged words fell after early 2024; 'significant' kept rising
finding: Words flagged as ChatGPT tells such as 'delve' dropped soon after being flagged in early 2024 while other LLM-favoured words kept rising, so word-count methods can undercount use.
limits: preprint; word frequencies, not usage

title: Empirical evidence of Large Language Model's influence on human spoken communication
measure: Frequency of ChatGPT-favoured words in 737,083 hours of unscripted podcast speech; synthetic control around ChatGPT release
latest_value: abrupt rise after ChatGPT (size not in abstract)
finding: Words ChatGPT favours, such as 'delve', rose abruptly in spontaneous spoken English after ChatGPT's release.
limits: preprint; word adoption, not views; also in group.jsonl

title: The Rise of AI-Generated Content in Wikipedia
measure: % of new English Wikipedia articles (Aug 2024) flagged AI at 1% false-positive calibration
finding: Over 5% of new English Wikipedia articles created in Aug 2024 were flagged as AI-generated, lower in other languages.
limits: new articles only; many deleted; covered in group pass

title: New user trends on Wikipedia
measure: Human pageviews to Wikipedia, year on year
finding: Human pageviews fell about 8% year on year in 2025, which the Foundation links to AI answers in search and social video.
limits: followed bot reclassification (Mar–Aug 2025); cause not isolated

title: Google users are less likely to click on links when an AI summary appears
measure: % of Google searches followed by a result click, with vs without AI summary (900 adults' browsing, Mar 2025)
latest_value: 8% vs 15%; 1% clicked a link in the summary
finding: Users clicked a result about half as often when an AI summary appeared.
limits: one month; query mix differs; Google disputes

title: Americans and AI 2026: chatbots, smart devices and views on impact
measure: % of US adults who ever read AI summaries at top of search results (n=5,119, 17–23 Feb 2026)
finding: Six in ten US adults say they read AI summaries at the top of search results.
limits: first time asked; 'ever' read; self-report

title: AI Overviews reduce clicks (update)
measure: Average desktop CTR of top-ranking page for keywords with vs without AI Overview (300,000 keywords, Search Console data)
finding: An AI Overview now goes with a 58% lower click-through rate for the top result, up from 34.5% in the previous year's study.
limits: SEO vendor; correlational; comparison window changed (1 vs 2 years)

title: Chartbeat 2026 Publisher Playbook: Google search referrals
measure: Year-on-year change in Google search referral traffic to publishers in Chartbeat's network
finding: Google search referrals to publishers fell 21.9% and then 40.2% in successive years to July 2026, while direct traffic's share rose from 13.5% to 15.9%.
limits: analytics vendor's client network; no site count; cause not isolated (algorithm updates, Discover)

title: Journalism and Technology Trends and Predictions 2026
measure: % change in Google search referrals to 2,500+ publisher sites
finding: Google search referrals to publishers fell a third in the year to Nov 2025.
limits: overlaps with Jul–Jul series; client network

title: Google zero-click searches 2026 study
measure: % of US Google searches ending without any click (panel clickstream)
finding: About 68% of US Google searches ended without a click in early 2026, up about 7.6 points from 2024.
limits: different panel providers across years; excludes Google app

title: Zero-click news searches
measure: % of news-related searches ending without a click
finding: Zero-click news searches rose from 56% to 69% in a year.
limits: panel estimate; vendor; no 2026 point found

title: AI Overviews study
measure: % of tracked keywords triggering an AI Overview
finding: AI Overviews appeared on 6.5% of tracked keywords in Jan 2025, peaked near 25% in July and fell to about 16% by November.
limits: not weighted by search volume; Google changes placement

cite: Alphabet Q1 2026 via Search Engine Journal
title: Google search revenue Q1 2026: AI Mode, record queries
measure: Google Search query volume (company statement); Search revenue growth
latest_value: queries at 'all-time high'; Search revenue +19% y/y (Q1 2026)
finding: Google said search queries hit an all-time high in Q1 2026, so searching has not shrunk even as clicks out fall.
limits: company statement, no figure

title: Digital News Report 2026: emerging uses of AI chatbots for news
measure: % of online adults in 48 markets using AI chatbots for news weekly; % naming AI as main source
latest_value: 10% weekly (7% in 2025); 1% main source; youngest 17% vs oldest 5% (2026)
finding: Weekly chatbot news use rose from 7% to 10% in a year, but only 1% name AI their main news source and 20% trust chatbot answers.
limits: online panels; excludes AI Overviews/AI Mode by definition; growth driven by Global South markets

title: Generative AI and News Report 2025
measure: % in 6 countries using generative AI weekly to get news; weekly use of any genAI
latest_value: 6% news (2025) vs 3% (2024); any weekly use 34% vs 18%
finding: Weekly use of generative AI for news doubled from 3% to 6% in six countries between 2024 and 2025.
limits: no 2026 wave found yet (2025 published 7 Oct)

title: Americans and AI 2026
measure: % of US adults who use AI chatbots, and for news, emotional support, companionship
latest_value: 49% use chatbots (33% in 2024); news 13%; emotional support 10%; companionship 4% (Feb 2026)
finding: Half of US adults now use chatbots, but only 13% have used them for news and 4% for companionship.
limits: 2024 question asked only of those aware of chatbots; purposes are 'ever'

title: ChatGPT weekly active users
measure: ChatGPT weekly active users (company statements)
finding: ChatGPT weekly users rose from 100m (Nov 2023) to about 1bn (Jul 2026).
limits: self-reported; use is mostly practical, not cultural

title: How People Use ChatGPT (NBER WP 34255)
measure: Classification of ChatGPT conversations by purpose
latest_value: practical guidance, seeking information and writing ≈80% of conversations
finding: Nearly 80% of ChatGPT conversations are practical guidance, information-seeking or writing, and non-work use rose above 70%.
limits: OpenAI co-authors and data

title: News Integrity in AI Assistants
measure: % of AI-assistant answers to news questions with at least one significant issue (3,000+ answers, 18 countries)
finding: Almost half of assistant answers to news questions had at least one significant problem.
limits: evaluators have a stake; models change fast

title: The crawl-to-click gap
measure: Pages crawled per referral sent back, by AI company
finding: AI crawlers take far more pages than they send visitors back, though ratios fell for some firms in 2025.
limits: Cloudflare sites only; sells the remedy

title: Talk, Trust, and Trade-Offs
measure: % of US teens 13–17 who have used / regularly use AI companions (broad definition)
finding: 72% of US teens have used an AI companion on a broad definition; 9% use one as a friend.
limits: advocacy group; broad definition; no 2026 wave found in this search

title: Teens, Social Media and AI Chatbots 2025
measure: % of US teens using AI chatbots, and for casual conversation or emotional support
latest_value: 64% use chatbots; 16% casual conversation; 12% emotional support (Sep–Oct 2025)
finding: 64% of US teens use chatbots, 12% for emotional support.
limits: first wave of these items

title: AI companion apps on track to pull in $120M in 2025
measure: Companion-app consumer revenue and downloads (337 apps)
finding: Companion-app revenue grew 64% and downloads 88% year on year in H1 2025.
limits: app-store estimates; spending not time; excludes web and general chatbots

title: Young adults leading the way in AI adoption
measure: % of US adults who have used AI for companionship
finding: 16% of US adults said they had used AI for companionship.
limits: one-off; wording broad

title: How people use Claude for support, advice and companionship
measure: % of Claude.ai conversations that are affective / companionship or role-play
finding: Companionship and role-play were under 0.5% of Claude.ai conversations.
limits: one general assistant; company data

cite: Fang et al. 2025 (MIT Media Lab & OpenAI)
title: How AI and Human Behaviors Shape Psychosocial Effects of Extended Chatbot Use: A Longitudinal Randomized Controlled Study
measure: Loneliness, socialising with people, emotional dependence, problematic use over 4 weeks (n=981, 300,000+ messages)
latest_value: no condition effects; heavier voluntary use linked to worse outcomes
finding: Chatbot mode and conversation type had no significant effect, but people who chose to use the chatbot more did worse on loneliness, socialising and dependence.
limits: 4 weeks; dose finding is correlational; OpenAI co-authors

title: AI Companions Reduce Loneliness
measure: Loneliness after interacting with AI companion vs human vs other activities; one-week longitudinal study
latest_value: loneliness reduced over one week; similar to talking with a person
finding: AI companions reduced loneliness about as much as talking with another person, and consistently over a week.
limits: short horizon; preprint as read

title: Trust in media (news release, 29 Sep 2026)
measure: % of US adults with great deal/fair amount of trust in mass media (n≈1,000, ±4)
finding: US trust in mass media rose from a record-low 28% in 2025 to 33% in 2026, driven by Republicans (8% to 22%).
limits: US; partisan swings; not tied to AI

title: Digital News Report 2026 executive summary
measure: % who trust most news most of the time; % worried about real vs fake online (48 markets, n=97,520)
finding: Trust in news fell to 37%, the lowest since 2015, and worry about telling real from fake rose to 62%.
limits: market set changes; not attributed to AI

title: Bad Bot Report series
measure: % of web requests on Imperva network from bots
finding: Bots made up 53% of web traffic in 2025, up from 37% in 2019 but below 2014's 59%.
limits: vendor network; requests not attention

title: SoA survey on generative AI (via The Bookseller)
measure: % of members who lost work / income to generative AI (n=787)
latest_value: illustrators 25% lost work, >33% income fell; translators >33% lost work, ~40% income fell
finding: A quarter of illustrators and over a third of translators said they had lost work to generative AI.
limits: self-selected union members; self-attribution

title: Who Is AI Replacing? The Impact of Generative AI on Online Freelancing Platforms
measure: Freelance job postings by category before/after ChatGPT and image generators
latest_value: declines in writing and image-related postings (size not read)
finding: Demand for freelance work in writing, coding and image categories fell after ChatGPT and image generators launched (effect sizes not read this session).
limits: one platform; postings not earnings

title: Global economic study shows human creators' future at risk from generative AI
measure: Share of music and audiovisual creators' revenues at risk by 2028; genAI content market
latest_value: 24% music, 21% audiovisual at risk by 2028; €22bn cumulative 2024–28; genAI market €3bn to €64bn
finding: Collecting societies forecast 24% of music creators' and 21% of audiovisual creators' revenues at risk by 2028.
limits: commissioned by rights bodies; scenario model

title: Gartner predicts search engine volume will drop 25% by 2026
measure: Traditional search engine volume by 2026
finding: Gartner forecast a 25% drop in traditional search volume by 2026; Google reports record query volume in 2026, though clicks out to sites have fallen.
limits: no baseline; volume vs clicks conflated in coverage

title: '90% of online content synthetically generated by 2026' (widely cited)
measure: Share of online content synthetically generated by 2026
latest_value: 90% (claimed); not found in Europol report as fetched (2024 revision)
finding: The widely repeated 90%-by-2026 claim was not found in the current Europol report; measured shares in 2026 are ~50% of new articles and 2.5% of pages purely AI.
limits: source trail unclear; may be in the original 2022 version

title: LEAP wave 3: daily AI companionship
measure: % of US adults using AI daily for companionship
finding: Experts forecast daily AI companionship rising to 15% of US adults by 2030 and 30% by 2040.
limits: expert judgement; read in 06_forecasts notes, not this session

title: AI models collapse when trained on recursively generated data
measure: Model quality across generations trained on prior models' output
finding: Training mostly on recursively generated data makes models lose the rare parts of the original distribution.
limits: replacement setting, not mixed data

title: Is Model Collapse Inevitable? Breaking the Curse of Recursion by Accumulating Real and Synthetic Data
measure: Test error across generations when synthetic data replaces vs accumulates with real data
finding: Collapse occurs when synthetic data replace real data but is avoided when they accumulate alongside it.
limits: lab settings; real web mix unknown

title: GPT detectors are biased against non-native English writers
measure: Detector misclassification of native vs non-native English writing
latest_value: non-native samples consistently misclassified as AI
finding: Several widely used detectors consistently flagged non-native English writing as AI while classing native writing correctly.
limits: 2023 detectors; newer vendors claim far lower false-positive rates

title: Algorithmic Effects on the Diversity of Consumption on Spotify
measure: Generalist-specialist diversity of listening, algorithmic vs organic (100m+ users, ~70bn streams, 2018–19)
finding: Algorithm-driven listening was less diverse than user-chosen listening, and users who became more diverse did so by moving away from recommendations.
limits: Spotify co-authors; associations only; pre-genAI recommender

title: Experimental study of inequality and unpredictability in an artificial cultural market
measure: Inequality and unpredictability of song success with vs without visible popularity signals (14,341 participants)
latest_value: social influence raised inequality and unpredictability
finding: Showing others' choices made cultural success more unequal and less predictable, the foundation for why ranking systems shape culture.
limits: foundation; pre-AI; artificial market

title: Gradual Disempowerment: Systemic Existential Risks from Incremental AI Development
measure: Proposed culture measures: human vs AI share of widely consumed content; human–AI relationships
finding: The paper asks for attention-weighted shares of AI content and measures of human–AI relationships, which remain the least measured parts of this stop.
limits: framework, no data
